title: Red Eye Treatment in Fort Myers | Riverside Family Eye Care
metaDescription: A red, gritty or aching eye, examined properly. Our optometrists name the cause, infection, allergy, dryness, injury or eye pressure, and treat it.
h1: Red eye treatment in Fort Myers, by doctors who find the cause, not just soothe the surface
html:
Your eye is red, gritty, or aching, and you honestly cannot tell what is behind it. Red eye treatment in Fort Myers starts with naming the cause, and Riverside Family Eye Care is a full-service optometry practice where our optometrists handle both the comprehensive and the medical side of eye care under one roof. So a red or sore eye gets looked at properly, the cause named, and the right care started, a calm exam, not a guess with leftover drops.

Request Appointment or call 239-500-2020.

Three things a real red-eye exam gives you

Not a shrug and a sample. A real answer on the cause, relief for the irritation, and a clear call on whether it is minor or urgent.

Know what is actually causing it

Redness is a symptom, not a diagnosis. The point of the visit is a real answer on what is behind it, an infection, an allergy, dryness, an injury, or pressure inside the eye, because the right treatment depends entirely on the cause. Drops that calm one of those can do nothing for another, which is why guessing at the bottle rarely works.

Get relief for the irritation

You do not have to live with the pain, the grittiness, and the light sensitivity while you wait to be seen. Call us and we will see you as soon as we can, and we treat the discomfort as part of the visit, not a shrug and a free sample, but care aimed at what is actually wrong.

Know whether it is minor or urgent

You leave knowing where you stand: whether this is a minor irritation that will pass with a little care, or something that needs closer watching or faster action. Our optometrists take the time to examine the eye and diagnose the cause rather than make a rushed guess, and if it has not settled, we bring you back for another look.

What the red-eye exam covers

Here is what the exam includes, step by step:

  • A focused history first, whether you wear contact lenses, whether there was an injury or a chemical splash, and how long the eye has been red, because the story often points straight at the cause.
  • A close look at the surface of the eye and the lids under magnification, so nothing on the front of the eye is missed.
  • A check for a trapped foreign body or a scratch on the cornea, the kind of thing that keeps an eye red until it is found.
  • A dye stain on the surface that lights up any abrasion underneath, so a small scratch does not hide behind the redness.
  • A measurement of the pressure inside the eye where the picture calls for it, since some red, aching eyes are a pressure problem rather than a surface one.
  • A treatment plan matched to what is actually found, not a one-size bottle sent home with everyone.

Red eye is one of the urgent eye problems we handle right here, alongside pink eye, foreign-body removal, and sudden flashes or floaters. And if the cause points to something a surgeon or a hospital has to handle, a deep injury, or a condition beyond what an office visit can settle, our optometrists tell you plainly and coordinate that care, rather than sitting on it.

Red, sore, and no way to tell how serious it is

Here is how it usually goes. Your eye turns red overnight, or it starts to feel gritty and sore through the day, and you genuinely cannot tell whether it is just allergies, a stray eyelash, a patch of dryness, or something that needs a doctor today. So it gets handled at home: wait it out, dig up an old bottle of drops, borrow someone else's, and eventually give up and sit for hours in a general ER waiting room that is not really built for eyes.

The trouble is that a red eye has many causes. Some are harmless and settle on their own. Some are infections, scratches, or pressure problems that can threaten your sight if they are left alone. From the outside they can look almost the same, and guessing wrong is the real risk.

That is the gap we close. Riverside Family Eye Care is here for the Fort Myers families and adults who want thorough, personal eye care, doctors who take the time to find out what is actually going on, rather than a rushed fix.

Why the retail counter and the ER both leave you waiting

The usual options do not fit a sudden red eye. A coupon-and-glasses retail counter or a rushed big-box chain can sell you a pair of frames, but it cannot examine or treat an eye that has turned red and sore. A general ER can help, but it often means hours in the waiting room to be seen by someone who does not work with eyes all day. Here, you reach a real eye doctor, one who examines the eye properly, names the cause, and follows up if it does not clear on the first visit.

Straight answers before you come in

Should I go to the ER or an eye doctor?

For most red eyes, an eye doctor is better equipped, we look at eyes all day and have the right tools to examine one properly. Save the ER for a chemical burn, a deep or penetrating injury, or sudden vision loss, for those, go to the ER or call 911 first. If what you have needs a surgeon, we will refer you and help coordinate that care rather than attempt it here.

Is it pink eye?

Maybe. Redness has many causes, and pink eye is only one of them, allergy, dryness, a scratch, or a trapped particle can all look similar from the outside. Sorting out which one it is, is exactly what the exam is for, so you treat the real problem instead of the wrong one.

Will I need a prescription?

It depends on what we find. Some red eyes need prescription drops to clear an infection or calm inflammation; some need only simple care and a little time. We prescribe when the cause calls for it, and we say so plainly when it does not.

Is the visit covered by insurance?

A red-eye visit is often medically billable, so it usually runs through your medical plan rather than a vision plan. Coverage depends on your specific plan, so give us a call and we will help you check before you come in. We do not post prices, because what you pay depends on your coverage.

What if it turns out to be serious?

Then you are in the right place to find out early. If the cause needs a surgeon or a hospital, our optometrists tell you plainly and coordinate your care from here. We do not perform eye surgery in our office, and we will not pretend every problem belongs here, but naming it fast is how the serious ones get handled in time.

More of the urgent eye care we handle

If you are not sure which problem you are dealing with, start here.

  • Emergency Eye Care: the full picture of the urgent eye problems we treat and manage.
  • Pink Eye (Conjunctivitis): for redness, discharge, and itching that may be an infection.
  • Foreign Body Removal: for a fleck of metal, grit, or debris caught in the eye.
  • Flashes & Floaters: for sudden sparks, a shower of specks, or a shadow in your vision.

Let's take a look

If your eye is red or sore right now, the fastest thing you can do is call. We will find out what is behind it and start the right treatment. Most red-eye visits are billable through your medical plan; we do not post prices because coverage varies, so call and we will walk you through it.
